case_title: State of A.P. v. M. Sohan Babu & Anr.
aggravating_circumstances: Accused entered at midnight armed with knives for robbery; knives used repeatedly; neighbours also injured and threatened
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.302/34, 460 and 324; sentence not stated in judgment
high_court_outcome: Conviction altered to IPC s.304 Part I; acquitted of s.302 (judgment dated 11.12.2003)
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 r/w s.34; also s.460 and s.324 (trial court judgment restored)
neutral_facts: In the early hours of 21 November 1991, two armed men entered a two-storey residential house occupied by an extended family, with the apparent purpose of robbery. The victim, a railway employee, lived on the ground floor with a spouse and children, while relatives and a neighbour lived in other portions of the building. Hearing footsteps, the victim came out and found the first accused standing on the first-floor balcony. A scuffle followed, and the noise woke other occupants, who saw the victim grappling with the accused and pinning the accused to the ground. The accused then drew a knife from a pocket and stabbed the victim in the left abdomen. When a relative came to help, the accused stabbed that relative in the right arm. The second accused came from the balcony, stabbed the victim on both thighs, held a knife at the throat of another relative to prevent help, and stabbed a further relative in the left shoulder. Two relatives overpowered the first accused and pushed the accused off the balcony. Neighbours arrived, seized the second accused, and both accused were tied with a rope on the ground floor. Police were informed. The victim was taken by car to a railway hospital but died on the way. The other injured persons were examined and given first aid; their injuries were found to be simple. The trial evidence consisted of eyewitness accounts from the relatives and medical evidence of the injuries.
physical_harm: Victim died of stab injuries (abdomen and both thighs); relatives and neighbours suffered stab injuries found to be simple
premeditation_planning: Not found; court described initial purpose as robbery and intent to kill as arising during the incident
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of the relatives and neighbours on the stabbing sequence and the injuries caused; medical evidence of injuries
witness_credibility: Not separately assessed; the Supreme Court treated the eyewitness and medical evidence as established and relied on it
trial_duration: offence: 20/21 November 1991; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 11.12.2003; Supreme Court: 14 December 2010
legal_representation: For the State (appellant): I. Venkatanarayana, Ramesh Allanki, D. Mahesh Babu. For the accused (respondents): Anil Kumar Tandale, Manoj C. Mishra, Brajesh Jha
investigation_status: Information sent to police; trial completed with conviction by trial court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302/34, 460, 324. High Court: conviction altered to s.304 Part I, acquitted of s.302. Supreme Court: High Court's s.304 part set aside; trial court judgment restored
prosecution_argument: State challenged the High Court's alteration of the s.302 conviction to s.304 Part I; the specific arguments are not recorded
legal_principle_applied: Common intention under s.34 may be inferred from circumstances as they arise during the incident; a blow in the course of an incident with knives used repeatedly does not fall under s.304 Part I
sentencing_rationale: Not stated; sentence restored from trial court judgment without separate sentencing reasoning
judicial_aggravating_factors: Accused entered armed at midnight for robbery; repeated knife use; neighbours injured and threatened
